evidence_items.locator: Section 'Full Self-Driving Capability', paragraph after the feature list

receipt.public_excerpt: The currently enabled Autopilot, Enhanced Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features require active driver supervision and do not make the vehicle autonomous.

evidence_items.explanation: Tesla's own support page from about January 2024 says even its Full Self-Driving features need active supervision and do not make the car autonomous. So new Teslas could not drive themselves.

evidence_items.publisher: Tesla, Inc. via NHTSA (Part 573 Safety Recall Report 23V-838)

receipt.public_excerpt:
When Autosteer is engaged, as with all SAE Level 2
advanced driver-assistance features and systems, the driver is the operator of
the vehicle.

evidence_items.explanation: In December 2023, Tesla's filing to the US safety regulator called its standard Autosteer a Level 2 driver-assistance feature, with the human as operator. The 2,031,220 vehicles in the recall include cars built through December 7, 2023.

receipt.public_excerpt: all of its vehicles, including Model 3, now include the hardware necessary for full self-driving capability, the company said.

evidence_items.explanation: Background on the 2016 promise that all new Teslas were built for full self-driving. It does not state the end-2017 date.

receipt.public_excerpt: After about a decade of promises and missed deadlines, Tesla still does not offer a vehicle that's safe to use without a human at the wheel ready to steer or brake at all times.

evidence_items.explanation: A later report saying the promise was still unmet in April 2025. It falls outside the target period, so it is context only.
